name: workbench-shell
title: Workbench shell
description: A tool layout with an explorer, canvas and inspector you can resize by mouse or keyboard, a toolbar, a status bar and sheets on phones.
docs: Pass canvas, and any of explorer, inspector, toolbar and status. The panels are separated from the canvas by drag handles that are also keyboard separators: focus one and press the arrow that moves it toward the canvas to grow its panel by 16px (Shift for 64), the other arrow to shrink it, Home to collapse it and End to bring it back. A double click on a handle brings its panel back to its starting width. Dragging a panel below half its minimum collapses it, and dragging out of the collapsed hairline opens it again. Two toggles in the toolbar collapse and restore the panels, and when the shell is narrower than 64rem (lg) they open the panels as sheets instead; breakpoint changes that width in rem, and it is never less than the panels' minimums and the canvas minimum need together; below it the panels are also hidden by CSS before the script has run, so a narrow screen never paints a squeezed layout first. The content of a panel is mounted once and moved between the panel and its sheet, so a field keeps what was typed and a tree keeps its open folders when a sheet closes or the shell crosses the breakpoint. The shell reads its own width, not the window's, so it works inside a pane, and it follows dir="rtl". The explorer and inspector scroll on their own; the canvas takes the room that is left, scrolls on its own, has min-width 0 so a wide editor or artboard can never push the layout out, and is a tab stop only while there is something to scroll. defaultSizes takes { explorer, inspector, collapsed } in px, minSizes the least width of the panels and of the canvas, and onSizesChange hands you the same shape once per gesture (a released drag, a key, a toggle; not a gesture that ends where it began), so it can go straight to localStorage and back into defaultSizes. Pass sizes to keep the layout yourself. When the shell is too narrow for the sizes you chose, the panels give way together and return to your sizes when it grows again. The toolbar slot sits between the toggles and scrolls sideways if it does not fit; status is a 28px strip that scrolls on a phone. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className.
